Congenital arteriovenous malformation of retinal blood vessels; cerebral involvement is not established for this isolated concept.
Inherited cardiomyopathy affecting myocardial structure and ventricular filling.
Fibrosarcoma arising in the breast; breast has no axis, regardless of stromal histology.
Intestinal magnesium malabsorption causes severe hypomagnesemia and secondary hypocalcemia; seizures in 2/5 do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Vascular lesions with thrombocytopenia; GI and skin lesions 80-99%. Lung lesions and intracranial bleeding 30-79% omitted by cap. Definition incorrectly describes a gene.
Benign nipple duct neoplasm of the breast, with superficial epidermal erosion; breast origin has no axis.
Severe central neurodevelopmental disorder; structural clubfoot and eyelid ptosis each reported in 1/1 patient, with limited frequency evidence.
Developmental shortening of digit bones; additional organs vary among syndromic subtypes.
Malignancy arising in the posterior urethra, part of the urinary tract.
Chlamydial bacterial infection umbrella; urinary, ocular and respiratory sites vary, with no single organ consistently affected across the group.
Complex spastic paraplegia with developmental disability and white-matter abnormalities; weakness is neurogenic, while individual skeletal deformities occur in 1/4.
Idiopathic edema of the cornea.
Defined by severe developmental delay, osteoporosis/osteosarcoma and diabetes; cataracts are a defining feature, frequency unreported. Macrocytosis omitted by cap.
Locally aggressive neoplasm of blood-vessel endothelium; no additional organ site is specified.
Juvenile motor-neuron degeneration; fixed joint contractures and scoliosis each occur in 2/3 reported patients, with skeletal muscle atrophy in 1/3.
Inherited renal resistance to vasopressin causes persistent urinary concentrating failure and disordered water balance; lasting brain injury is not established as common.
Balantidium infection of the large intestine causing colitis and dysentery.
Benign granular cell nerve-sheath neoplasm, classified here as a peripheral nervous system tumor; anatomical sites vary.
Primary narrowing of pulmonary veins; pulmonary vascular obstruction belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Malignancy of the submandibular salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Vascular tumor-associated platelet consumption and coagulopathy define the syndrome; petechiae and purpura are bleeding signs, and hepatic lesions occur in 5-29%.
Progressive epileptic encephalopathy with dystonia and neurodegeneration; recurrent respiratory infections are separate illnesses, and optic atrophy occurs in 1-4%.
Reported enzyme-deficiency syndrome with elevated lactate/pyruvate and a neurodevelopmental phenotype including delay and chorea; frequency data are unavailable.
